frameworks.name: Reinforcement-Based Behavioral Causation
frameworks.definition: Behavior is determined entirely by the consequences (reward or punishment) that follow action; people repeat behaviors that produce favorable outcomes and avoid those that produce negative ones, independent of their origins or circumstances.

claims.text: Childhood adversity does not directly cause adult success or failure. Many people experience difficult childhoods and achieve nothing, while others do the same and succeed. The outcome is determined not by the trauma itself but by the behavioral patterns that follow.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: The only law of human behavior is that people repeat actions for which they are rewarded and avoid actions for which they are punished, regardless of when those reinforcement patterns originated.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Raising your minimum standard produces a feedback loop where you continue to work harder, because the better outcomes that follow reinforce that higher standard, which then sets expectations for the next level of achievement.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Achieving better outcomes from higher standards reinforces the new standard, creating a self-reinforcing escalation cycle

claims.text: People succeed not because of their origins but because they have been reinforced over time for the specific behaviors that produce results, meaning focus should be on understanding and replicating the behavioral inputs of high performers rather than attributing success to their circumstances.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: Many people face difficult circumstances growing up. Some become successful and some do not. The fact that outcomes diverge despite similar starting conditions proves that the childhood circumstance itself is not the determining factor.

practices.text: Focus on the observable behaviors and reinforcement patterns of high performers rather than asking them to explain their success, because post-hoc explanations do not reveal the true causal mechanisms of habitual behavior.
Deliberately raise your minimum standard in your craft and work intentionally to maintain that new floor, allowing the reinforcement from improved outcomes to drive continued escalation.
